summary: A 1940 CCC-built steel tower on Grand Canyon's North Rim, no longer used for fire detection, listed on the register in 2009.

facts.design: International Derrick (IDEOC) 7x7 steel tower and cab, about 82 ft 6 in high
facts.status_note: Inactive; no longer used for fire detection (NHLR, NPS)

access.note: Remote part of the North Rim inside Grand Canyon National Park. The sources describe no public trail, road to the base, or visitor rule.

events.note: Constructed by the CCC in one of the last major projects the corps completed in the park (NPS). NHLR gives 'Built 1940'.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, April 25, 2009
The four Grand Canyon lookout towers were recognized at a ceremony with the opening of the North Rim Wildland Fire and Emergency Services Facility, July 4, 2009

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR and NPS give 82 ft 6 in (about 25.1 m). The peak-bagging page gives 83 ft. The register and NPS figure is used.

The NPS article says the National Park Service built the Kanabownits tower, while the entry for the tower itself says the CCC constructed it in 1940. The story names the CCC as builder and the NPS as administrator.

sources.title: Four Grand Canyon National Park Lookout Towers have been listed on the National Historic Lookout Register

notes_for_editor: NHLR and NPS agree on the 1940 date, the CCC build, the 82 ft 6 in height and the inactive status. Access is unknown because no source describes a route, trail or visitor rule. The unstaffed status rests on the 2009 NPS article and NHLR wording, not a current check. The peak-bagging photo is cited only for its date; its license was not checked, so no photo was added to the record.
